concepts.title: KV cache memory math
concepts.body: Per token, the cache stores 2 (K and V) x num_layers x num_kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_element. For a 70B-class model with 80 layers, 8 KV heads (GQA), head_dim 128 and fp16, that is 2 x 80 x 8 x 128 x 2 = ~327 KB per token. A 32k-token sequence costs ~10 GB, per request. This is why GQA, quantized KV cache and paged attention exist, and why serving capacity is bounded by memory rather than FLOPs.

concepts.title: Prefill vs decode
concepts.body: Prefill processes the whole prompt in parallel and is compute-bound. Decode generates one token at a time, reads all weights and the whole KV cache per token, and is memory-bandwidth-bound. Time to first token (TTFT) is dominated by prefill, inter-token latency by decode. Optimizations differ: batching and chunked prefill help throughput; speculative decoding and quantization help decode latency.
